statements.quote:
To address this research question, we conducted a pre-registered
randomized controlled experiment (𝑁= 486).

We independently
validated our findings on LLM-enabled co-creation in the more nat-
uralistic setting of product ideation (i.e., in a second, preregistered
experiment with 𝑁= 640 participants).

To empirically assess our hypotheses, we performed a preregistered
(https://aspredicted.org/nf5r-cmrt.pdf) randomized controlled ex-
periment with 𝑁= 502 participants.

Codes and anonymized data
are available via our GitHub (https://github.com/SM2982/replication-
creativity-CHI2026).

Data were collected and
stored in accordance with local data privacy laws.
The full list of prompts is provided in Appendix A.

To account for potential exclusions such as due to
attention checks, we aimed for 100 participants per group as prereg-
istered.

Following
our preregistered exclusion criteria, we removed participants who
failed at least one attention check (10 participants), acknowledged
unauthorized AI use during the study (2 participants), provided
nonsense answers (2 participants), participated more than once (1
participant), or did not finish the questionnaire (1 participant).

The detailed
coding scheme can be found in the Appendix E.

Full measurement details, including all
exploratory instruments and item wordings, are provided in the
public GitHub repository.

Our preregistered one-sided hypotheses
were tested via contrasts of estimated marginal means.

All analyses were conducted in R 4.4.1, using the emmeans package
[53] for calculating the contrasts.

To test the robustness of our results and their generalizability to
another domain, we conducted a preregistered replication study
(https://aspredicted.org/de6md8.pdf).

All adapted prompts used in
this validation study are provided in Appendix A.

As in the initial study, we evaluated our preregistered directional
hypotheses at 𝛼= .05, applied Holm-adjusted 𝑝-values to control
the family-wise error rate, and used simple linear regressions for
our analyses regarding idea diversity and perceived idea ownership.

The questionnaire, analysis code, and anonymized data are pub-
licly available in a GitHub repository: https://github.com/SM2982/
replication-creativity-CHI2026.

Detailed diagnostic plots for all
dependent variables can be found in our GitHub.

Arm counts: feedback=96 (Question-mode), suggestion=95, improvement=101 (Model-led), vanilla=95, control=99, matching Table 2. The code confirms the label mapping. There are 389 initial texts. The file also supplies Rater1-Rater4 and initial/final diversity scores. Columns: participant_id, Condition, Initial.idea, Conversation, Refined.idea, Rater1, Rater2, Overall. Joining to the main file by participant_id matches 79 records, with no arm disagreement; exact final-text matching also finds 79. The original reported correlation sample remains unresolved; the current files allow correlations on 79 matched records.

analysis/Study2/Data/data_full_anonymized.csv: 640 distinct rows and 640 unique final texts. Arm counts: feedback=97, suggestion=99, improvement=151, generation=99, vanilla=95, control=99. The code labels improvement 'Model-Led' and generation 'Generation-Mode'; the paper calls the additional arm model-led iterative. Idea_Quality, originality_mean, usefulness_mean, purchase_intent_mean and refined_div_condition are complete. Idea_Quality equals (originality_mean + usefulness_mean)/2 to floating-point precision. There are 543 nonmissing unique initial texts. submission_id has 543 nonmissing unique values; study_id has 458 distinct values across 640 rows and is not a unique person key; Submission.id has 638 nonmissing unique values, with two missing. The 640 rows support the paper's one-final-idea-per-person descriptive analysis, but study_id alone cannot verify distinct-person counts or safely link records.

analysis/Study2/Data/data_evaluators_honest_anonymized.csv: 6300 rows; 6300 unique evaluation_id, 640 unique idea_id, 258 unique evaluator_study_id, and 458 unique participant_study_id values. Columns: evaluation_id, evaluator_study_id, evaluator_honesty_answer, idea_id, participant_study_id, bot_type, originality, usefulness, purchase_intent, evaluation_order, time_spent_seconds, rater_num. Each idea has 6-13 ratings; the main file's rater_count sums to 6300. The long file supplies arms and originality, usefulness and purchase_intent ratings. The paper describes 320 raters rating 20 ideas each; its recruited rater count cannot be inferred from these public pseudonymous IDs. The files do not establish whether nonunique subject/rater identifiers reflect anonymization or another processing step.

Purchase intent is supplied as one mean per idea, and the R script groups purchase_intent_mean by bot_type. Observed arm means are 2.499864300526552 for improvement and 2.2428820618214558 for generation. These support checking the Section 6.3/Figure 8 attribution discrepancy, without silently relabeling the data.

Study 1's NPZ has 391 initial and 488 final 3072-dimensional vectors, with integer positional indices only, versus 389 initial texts and 486 final rows in the public CSV. Direct archive-to-CSV alignment is not confirmed; two extra final embeddings need reconciliation. Study 2's NPZ has 543 initial and 640 final 3072-dimensional vectors. Final indices are 0-639. Recomputing all-idea and within-arm leave-one-out cosine distances in CSV row order matches both saved columns to less than 0.000000000001, confirming final-vector alignment. Archives were read with numpy allow_pickle=False.

Code uses scipy.spatial.distance.cosine (distance, not similarity). Study 1 main quality/diversity analyses use lm; Study 2 quality uses lmer with idea_id and evaluator_study_id random intercepts, diversity uses lm, and clmm is a quality robustness check. Both R scripts use model residual sigma in emmeans::eff_size. These are code observations, not a claim that every published statistic has been reproduced. Complete pre-exclusion randomized-arm counts are not confirmed. The tree contains analysis/embedding code, questionnaire/rater materials and diagnostics, but no experimental assignment application source.

Public preregistration #237783, 'Exploring various LLM designs to augment human creativity', registered 2025-07-11. Describes five planned conditions, outcomes, analyses, exclusions and a target of at least 100 completed participants per group (at least 500 total). The cited .pdf URL returns public HTML (HTTP 200). Its ordinary Download PDF link returned a two-page PDF (HTTP 200); filename comes from Content-Disposition, size from downloaded bytes. No participant records, realized arm assignments, outcomes or participant idea texts are deposited here. Planned conditions are not observed assignment data. No explicit deposit license identified.

what_we_could_compute: Per-arm means, sample SDs, SEs and analyzed output/participant-row counts for S1-O1/S1-O2 and S2-O1/S2-O2/S2-O3. In particular, the missing Study 2 quality/diversity descriptives and arm sizes are recoverable from 640 rows with complete scores and arms (open questions 1 and 7). Study 2 identifiers require the limitations in the deposit notes; 458 unique study_id values must not replace its 640 analyzed rows.

For open question 2, compute Study 2 purchase-intent summaries by actual bot_type codes and check the conflicting arm attributions. For open question 13, calculate output-level summaries and SEs from purchase_intent_mean; individual ratings are also public in the 6300-row evaluator file.

For open questions 4 and 7, compute AI-versus-control diversity differences from existing individual cosine-distance scores, and new diversity measures from all final texts. Study 2's aligned final embeddings support pairwise/centroid measures and uncertainty calculations that recompute centroids under resampling. Study 1's 488-vector archive is not confirmed to align with its 486-row CSV, so new text embeddings or a verified mapping are needed before reusing that archive.

For open questions 3, 5 and 10, inspect the posted model specifications and residual-SD effect-size standardizer, and fit analyses to obtain contrast SEs, confidence intervals and effect sizes absent from the main tables. Original numerical reproduction, especially rater-clustered Study 2 models, is not assured until identifier issues are resolved.

For open question 11, calculate S1-O3 paired diversity changes, arm means/SDs/SEs and available-case counts for 292 participants (96 question, 95 suggestion, 101 model-led). This establishes the public file's count but does not explain the paper's t(295).

For open question 12, calculate S1-O4 elaboration distributions and arm means/SDs/SEs from 80 coded records, plus correlations with main outcomes for the 79 records joining by participant_id. The original correlation's analysis sample is still not established.
